- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.67) or volatile, model underestimates; increase forecast by 10–25% for next 3–7 days.
- Model often overshoots after sharp sentiment spikes (e.g., +1.00 followed by +0.67); cap forecast at 1.2x historical mean for 2–3 days post-spike.
- Forecasts show strong mean reversion bias: if 3+ consecutive days show high forecast error, adjust toward recent 7-day average.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overpredicts in early days (1–5) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply downward bias of 5–15% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– swings, model tends to lag; add 0.1–0.3 to forecast for each 2-day sentiment cycle.
